title: Aurumix: Revenue Model Explainer
subtitle: How the seven-year revenue, cost and funding model works, what it assumes and why, and how to use it.
tagline: Built by founders. Designed for founders.
legal: Prepared by Tokenomics.net for Aurumix. © 2026. Confidential.

intro: The workbook models Aurumix from 2027 to 2033: customers in the UAE, Oman and Bahrain, and India, the gold they hold, six revenue streams, the cost base and the funding need. Headcount and tax are not yet in the costs, so every profit figure is an upper bound.

findings.title: Three sources carry the revenue
findings.body: In Y7 the B2B platform fee is 34.7% of revenue, the SIP entry fee 29.5% and cardholder fees 21.2%. The family plan adds 10.0%, the spot entry fee 2.4%, and interchange and lending 2.3% between them.

findings.title: Customers who stop paying still count
findings.body: A customer who stops contributing keeps their gold, their card and their credit line. By Y7 the book holds 71,208 paying customers and 130,638 holders, and the vault holds 403,565 grams worth USD 91.1m.

findings.title: B2B partners are the largest single uncertainty
findings.body: The five most sensitive inputs are all B2B inputs. With 5 partners by Y7 instead of 11, Y7 is roughly at break-even and the funding need rises to USD 3.23m. The first signed partner term sheet is the most valuable evidence the model could receive.

findings.title: The profit line is an upper bound
findings.body: Salaries, legal and trust costs and tax sit only inside a 15% contingency. A 30% contingency alone cuts Y7 profit from USD 0.85m to USD 0.37m. The real headcount figure will matter more than any other single input.
